producer_report.summary: Admission now scans only the request's own text for boundary words. The root cause was in reading.rs: scan_request_input also read every file the request names, so naming BRIEF.md refused the request. The named-file loop and the git and treeish parameters are removed. The scan now takes the text and returns a Vec of findings. refuse_banned_input, its message and the doc comments say request-only, and ask and queue are updated. The old run/mod.rs test is replaced by two tests: a request naming BRIEF.md and docs/dirty.md (both holding a banned word) is admitted by queue and ask, and a request with a banned word on line 2 is still refused with 'not admitted' and 'request:2: <word>'. CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under Unreleased > Changed. I also updated docs/enforcement.md (row M19) and one comment in xtask/tests/policy.rs, because they named the old behavior and the deleted test. Word lists, boundary_scan and the scan of files a candidate changes are untouched.

checks_run.note: 51 passed, including the two new tests and the kept banned-word-in-request test
First run failed: docs/enforcement.md named the deleted test. Fixed; 12 of 12 pass on rerun.

criteria_check.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core shows that a request naming an existing file with a boundary word (such as BRIEF.md or a docs file) but whose own text has none is admitted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria_check.evidence: New test a_request_naming_a_file_with_a_boundary_word_is_admitted in run/mod.rs commits BRIEF.md and docs/dirty.md with a banned word, then asserts scan_request_input is empty and that queue and ask both admit the request (head moves, reading is Some). It passed in `cargo test --locked -p athena-core request_`. Under the old file loop it would have failed.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows that a request whose own text holds a boundary word is still refused with a 'not admitted' error naming source `request`. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria_check.evidence: New test a_request_whose_own_text_has_a_boundary_word_is_refused: the request names BRIEF.md and has the word on line 2. ask and queue both fail with 'not admitted' and 'request:2: <word>', head is unchanged, and the direct scan returns one finding with source `request`. It passed in the same run.

criteria_check.criterion: `scan_request_input` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs no longer reads named files at admission, and its doc comment and the `refuse_banned_input` message describe request-only scanning. The old test in run/mod.rs that expected a named dirty file to be refused is replaced.
criteria_check.evidence: scan_request_input(text) -> Vec<InputFinding> now only maps boundary_scan(text); the git, treeish and request_text_touches loop are gone. The doc comments of InputFinding, scan_request_input and refuse_banned_input and the bail message ('its own text holds words ...') say request-only. The old test a_named_file_with_a_banned_word_... is deleted and replaced by the two new tests.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks for the full `cargo test`. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (both pass), `cargo test --locked -p athena-core request_` and `cargo test --locked -p xtask --test policy` (both pass).

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry saying admission scans only the request's own text, not the files it names, and says why: the owner's brief legitimately uses boundary words.
criteria_check.evidence: New first bullet under [Unreleased] > Changed. It says admission (`athena ask`, including `--later`) scans only the request's own text; the owner's brief legitimately uses boundary words; a request to map it was refused on 2026-10-29; files are still scanned when a candidate changes them. It contains no banned words, and the policy scan passes.

criteria_check.criterion: The change refuses fewer readings, not more; no new refusal rule is added. Expected 0% of newly refused readings.
criteria_check.evidence: The diff only deletes the named-file loop and the git parameters. No new bail! or condition was added. The request-text scan uses the same boundary_scan and word lists, so the refusal set is a strict subset of the old one.

open_issues: admission.rs is a listed deliverable but is unchanged, because it holds no boundary scan.

I also edited docs/enforcement.md (row M19) and a comment in xtask/tests/policy.rs, neither in the deliverables list. They described the old behavior, and the policy test needed the enforcement row updated.
mistakes: My first policy run failed because I deleted the old test without updating docs/enforcement.md. I fixed that.
My first edit of the old test failed on a mistyped request string; I corrected it.
learnings: The M19 row in docs/enforcement.md names tests, and the xtask policy test every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists fails if a named test is deleted or renamed. Any rename needs that row updated.
The boundary scan at admission lives in reading.rs; admission.rs holds no scan.
